# OAuth broker

<!-- Generated by `go run docs/roadmap/gen.go docs` from tickets.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

**Phase:** [P3 · Act as the user](../README.md#phase-3--act-as-the-user) · **Lane:** Control plane · **Label:** `feature:oauth-broker` · **Epic:** [#132](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/132) · **Tickets:** 9 (5S 4M)

The CP runs OAuth authorization code + PKCE flows to third-party providers for signed-in employees, starting with Google and GitHub. Tokens go only to the CP-only user credential store `consent.store` (W-P3-CSIG-06; aws, or vault once W-P3-PUS-01 lands) under users/<userKey>/<provider>; workers never hold a credential for that store, the CP is the only party that refreshes or revokes a grant, and the CP database keeps only grant, pending and attempt metadata.

## How we build it

- Gate and back-compat: the broker is mounted only when the CP-local `consent.providers` list is non-empty, the cpstate DB from W-P1-SSO-01 is open (--state-dir), the consent sign-in block (W-P3-CSIG-01) is configured, and `consent.store` (W-P3-CSIG-06) is configured and persistent (aws today, vault after W-P3-PUS-01). With no store or an echo store and providers set, CP startup fails with `oauth broker requires a persistent consent.store`, because EchoStore.Get returns the key itself. With no providers, no routes, migrations, goroutines or wire fields are added.
- Provider config (CP-local, never on /policy): `consent.providers[]` {id passing secrets.ValidProviderID (W-P3-CSIG-06), type google|github|githubApp|generic, clientID, exactly one of clientSecretEnv or clientSecretKey (`oauth-clients/<id>` in consent.store, W-P3-BRKR-06), authURL, tokenURL, revokeURL, userinfoURL, allowedScopes[], defaultScopes[] (subset of allowedScopes), extraAuthParams, allowedAccountDomains[], requireEmailMatch}. `consent.connect.redirectURL` defaults to the origin of consent.oidc.redirectURL plus /connect/callback; `consent.connect.pendingTTL` defaults to 15m (allowed 1m-1h) and is also the JIT pending TTL (W-P3-JIT-01). Either secret source works for every type, because only the CP refreshes (W-P3-PUS-03). githubApp requires empty allowedScopes (permissions come from the app). extraAuthParams may not set client_id, redirect_uri, response_type, scope, state, code_challenge, code_challenge_method, nonce or include_granted_scopes.
- Built-in endpoints, overridable (for GitHub Enterprise Server): google auth https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth, token https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token, revoke https://oauth2.googleapis.com/revoke, params access_type=offline and prompt=consent; github and githubApp auth https://github.com/login/oauth/authorize, token https://github.com/login/oauth/access_token, revoke https://api.github.com/applications/{client_id}/grant, userinfo https://api.github.com/user. generic requires authURL and tokenURL, all https except loopback.
- Key layout: every key comes from the W-P3-CSIG-06 helpers: userKey = secrets.UserKey(iss, sub) (32 hex characters of a domain-separated SHA-256 over iss and sub) and secrets.UserGrantKey(userKey, provider) = `users/<userKey>/<provider>` in consent.store. With the default namePrefix the AWS name is `warden-cp/users/<userKey>/<provider>`, and no email or raw sub reaches a secret name. The reserved prefixes `users/`, `idp/`, `revoking/` and `oauth-clients/` are owned by W-P3-CSIG-06 (config validation, storeFetcher and /central/secrets); W-P3-BRKR-06 adds the worker-local /dashboard/api/secretstore.
- Data model (cpstate migrations oauthbroker/0001..0003, behind a GrantStore interface with a conformance suite for p5-postgres-ha): `pending_authorizations(id, iss, sub, user_key, agent_id NULL, provider, scopes_json, message NULL, request_method NULL, request_host NULL, request_path NULL, mcp_tool NULL, status pending|granted|denied|expired, reason, created_at, expires_at, completed_at)` is the long-lived intent shared with W-P3-JIT-01, which fills the request columns shown on the W-P3-PORT-03 landing page. `connect_attempts(state_hash PK, pending_id NULL, user_key, iss, sub, provider, scopes_json, verifier, browser_hash, created_at, expires_at +10m)` is one browser attempt, consumed once with DELETE ... RETURNING, like W-P1-SSO-03 oidc_pending (plaintext in the 0600 cpstate file; no extra encryption key). `oauth_grants(user_key, iss, sub, provider, grant_id, state connecting|active|reconsent_required|revoked, scopes_json, provider_account_id, provider_account_login, granted_at, updated_at, last_used_at, revoked_at, UNIQUE(user_key, provider))`. reconsent_required is set by the W-P3-PUS-03 refresh engine; the name leaves `grants` to the P4 delegation grants. No table has a column that can hold a token.
- Start: `POST /connect/start` (form fields provider, scopes, pending, csrf) behind the W-P3-CSIG-04 portal session middleware, CSRF = the session's X-Warden-CSRF value as header or form field plus an Origin check. GET only redirects (303) to the PORT-03 landing page or /portal and changes nothing. Checks in order: provider exists; user not blocked (BlockChecker over controlplane.BlockStore, fail closed 503); a given pending belongs to this (iss, sub) (otherwise 404 identical to unknown) and is open; scopes ⊆ allowedScopes and, with a pending, ⊆ pending.scopes, else defaultScopes (400 scope_not_allowed before any row is written). The per-agent cap is applied when the pending is created (W-P3-JIT-01), so the broker trusts pending.scopes and needs no dependency on per-user secrets; without a pending, a caller may pass an extra ceiling (the portal passes allowedScopes ∩ the union of perUserSecrets scopes, W-P3-PORT-03). The exported Broker.Start returns the provider URL and is shared by POST /connect/start (303) and the portal JSON actions. The request asks for the union of the active grant's scopes and the new scopes. Rate limit 10/minute per user_key (internal/ratelimit, moved from W-P2-TOKX-04) and at most 20 open attempts per user.
- Callback and write order: `GET /connect/callback` consumes the attempt by state hash, requires the browser cookie hash and the current portal session's (iss, sub) to match (403 before any code exchange), re-checks the block list, and exchanges code + verifier with golang.org/x/oauth2 (W-P1-SSO-03) using Accept: application/json, 10s timeout, no redirects and a 64 KiB cap; a 200 response with an `error` field is a failure. Then: (1) upsert oauth_grants with state=connecting and a new grant_id; (2) Put the oauthbroker.TokenRecord JSON at secrets.UserGrantKey(userKey, provider) in consent.store {v:1, grant_id, provider, client_id, token_type, access_token, refresh_token, scope, expiry (absolute UTC, 0 when the token never expires), refresh_expiry, obtained_at}, keeping the stored refresh_token when the response has none; (3) set state=active with the returned scopes; (4) re-check the block list and, if blocked now, delete the key and revoke the grant; (5) complete the pending, which notifies subscribers. The previous token is never revoked on reconnect, because Google revoke ends the whole grant. The callback, the refresh engine (W-P3-PUS-03), RevokeUserGrant (W-P3-PORT-02) and offboarding all take oauthbroker.GrantLocks, one mutex per (userKey, provider).
- Scopes: provider scope strings are parsed on spaces or commas. Granted scopes outside the cap (plus openid and email for account identity) mean nothing is stored (reason scope_exceeded). Granted scopes missing requested ones are stored as returned and the pending is marked denied with reason insufficient_scope so JIT callers stop retrying. A grant's token carries the union of its scopes; the per-agent cap is a consent-time ceiling and per-request limits come from egress policy.
- Account identity: after the exchange the broker records the provider account (Google id_token sub, email and hd read from the token endpoint response; GitHub GET /user id and login; generic userinfoURL when set) and enforces optional allowedAccountDomains and requireEmailMatch (account email equals the portal session's verified email). A mismatch denies with reason account_not_allowed, and the token is dropped and revoked.
- Refresh: workers never refresh and never receive provider metadata, client secrets or refresh tokens. W-P3-BRKR-07 adds the CP-side refresh_token client that the W-P3-PUS-03 engine calls, next to the code exchange (W-P3-BRKR-04) and revoke (W-P3-BRKR-05) clients, so every provider HTTP call lives in internal/oauthbroker and nothing is added to /policy or the signed bundle.
- Failure modes: provider down fails the attempt and leaves the pending open for retry. Secret backend failure after the code exchange drops the token from memory, leaves the grant connecting and returns 503 secret_store_unavailable. A 1-minute sweeper (not the hourly analytics retention ticker) prunes attempts, expires pendings and moves `connecting` grants older than 10m to revoked after deleting any key; an hourly pass flags keys under users/ with no active grant. GetPending reports expired lazily. JIT status waiters are in memory per replica (documented for p5-postgres-ha).
- Audit and observability: when admin audit is enabled, adminaudit.Recorder.Record gets connect.granted, connect.denied and connect.revoked with the new auth_method `portal`, target `grant:<provider>`, target_ref `grant_id:<id>` and details {provider, scopes, pending_id, provider_account_id}; an unhealthy Recorder fails the callback with 503 before the code exchange. No secrets.Ref, token, code, state, verifier or client secret appears in any row or log line. In-memory counters warden_cp_oauth_connect_total{provider,stage,outcome}, warden_cp_oauth_token_exchange_seconds{provider}, warden_cp_oauth_revoke_total{provider,outcome} and gauges for open pendings and orphaned grants are added to the W-P5-RETN-06 export list; labels use configured provider ids only.

## Done when

With `consent.providers` and a persistent consent.store (aws, or vault) configured, a signed-in employee connects Google and GitHub through POST /connect/start and GET /connect/callback; the versioned token JSON with its grant_id lands at users/<userKey>/<provider> in consent.store (warden-cp/users/... on AWS), and a scan of the cpstate file finds no token bytes. A callback from another portal session, a blocked user, a scope outside the cap, a replayed state, an account outside allowedAccountDomains and a missing or echo consent.store at startup are all refused with no secret written. Reconnecting without a refresh_token keeps the stored one, static placeholders and secret-store writes under reserved prefixes are rejected, a stored grant refreshes through the CP provider client, and with no providers configured the CP behaves exactly as today.

### 1/9 · W-P3-BRKR-01

**Add provider config model with Google and GitHub defaults**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#133](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/133)

Add `consent.providers[]` and `consent.connect` to the CP-local consent block and a provider Registry in new package internal/oauthbroker, with built-in endpoints for google, github and githubApp. Also add the shared scope helpers and the redacting token record type that every later P3 ticket uses; user keys come from W-P3-CSIG-06. Nothing is mounted, so behaviour does not change.

**Requirements**

- Config fields: id passing secrets.ValidProviderID (W-P3-CSIG-06), unique, type google|github|githubApp|generic, clientID, exactly one of clientSecretEnv or clientSecretKey (must equal `oauth-clients/<id>`), authURL, tokenURL, revokeURL, userinfoURL, allowedScopes, defaultScopes (subset of allowedScopes), extraAuthParams, allowedAccountDomains, requireEmailMatch; plus `consent.connect.redirectURL` and `consent.connect.pendingTTL` (default 15m, allowed 1m-1h; W-P3-JIT-01 uses it too). Strict parsing; the block never appears on /policy.
- Validation: URLs absolute https unless loopback; generic needs authURL and tokenURL; githubApp needs empty allowedScopes; scopes contain no whitespace or commas; extraAuthParams rejects client_id, redirect_uri, response_type, scope, state, code_challenge, code_challenge_method, nonce and include_granted_scopes. redirectURL defaults to the origin of consent.oidc.redirectURL plus /connect/callback and must end in /connect/callback. Errors name the field path.
- Defaults by type, each overridable: google auth https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth, token https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token, revoke https://oauth2.googleapis.com/revoke, access_type=offline, prompt=consent; github and githubApp auth https://github.com/login/oauth/authorize, token https://github.com/login/oauth/access_token, revoke https://api.github.com/applications/{client_id}/grant, userinfo https://api.github.com/user. Do not import golang.org/x/oauth2/google.
- Client secrets: clientSecretEnv is read at startup and a missing variable is a fatal error naming the variable; clientSecretKey is read through an injected SecretResolver (wired to consent.store by W-P3-BRKR-06), and a read failure logs WARN and is retried on first use (503 provider_unavailable). Secrets live in a type whose String, GoString and LogValue redact them.
- Shared helpers: `oauthbroker.ParseScopes` (space or comma separated) and `CapScopes(requested, allowed) (capped, rejected)`; `oauthbroker.TokenRecord` {v, grant_id, provider, client_id, token_type, access_token, refresh_token, scope, expiry, refresh_expiry, obtained_at} with Marshal/Parse (unknown versions rejected) and redacting String and LogValue. TokenRecord is the only stored grant format: W-P3-BRKR-04 writes it, W-P3-PUS-03 refreshes it and W-P3-PORT-02 reads it for provider revoke.
- The registry is fixed after startup (change needs a CP restart, as for the console block). One startup INFO line `oauth_providers_loaded ids=[...]`; configs without consent.providers load and serve exactly as before.

**Implementation plan**

1. internal/config consent block (added by W-P3-CSIG-01): add OAuthProviderConfig and ConsentConnectConfig with strict-field registration and validation as in the existing secretstore config.
2. New internal/oauthbroker/provider.go: Provider, the defaults table, NewRegistry(cfgs, SecretResolver), Get(id) returning ErrUnknownProvider, and sorted List().
3. New internal/oauthbroker/scopes.go: ParseScopes and CapScopes, sorted and de-duplicated.
4. New internal/oauthbroker/token.go: TokenRecord{V, GrantID, Provider, ClientID, TokenType, AccessToken, RefreshToken, Scope, Expiry, RefreshExpiry, ObtainedAt} with redacting String/LogValue.
5. Tests: provider_test.go, scopes_test.go, token_test.go and an internal/config consent provider validation test.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] A google provider with only id, type, clientID and clientSecretKey gets the documented Google URLs and access_type=offline, prompt=consent. Verify with `go test ./internal/oauthbroker -run TestRegistryDefaults`.
- [ ] A generic provider without tokenURL, a duplicate id, an id starting with `_`, a non-loopback http URL, extraAuthParams with redirect_uri or include_granted_scopes, or a githubApp with allowedScopes fails validation with an error naming the field path. Verify with `go test ./internal/config -run TestConsentProvidersValidate`.
- [ ] Registry.Get("unknown") returns ErrUnknownProvider and List returns only the configured ids, sorted.
- [ ] TokenRecord JSON round-trips with v 1 and Parse rejects an unknown version. Verify with `go test ./internal/oauthbroker -run TestTokenRecord`.
- [ ] slog JSON, %v and %#v output of Provider and TokenRecord contain no client secret or token value.

### 2/9 · W-P3-BRKR-02

**Add pending authorization, attempt and grant metadata stores**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#134](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/134)

Add cpstate migrations for pending_authorizations, connect_attempts and oauth_grants behind a GrantStore interface in internal/oauthbroker, with a conformance suite so a Postgres store can replace it later. The pending row is the long-lived intent shared with W-P3-JIT-01; each browser attempt gets its own single-use row like W-P1-SSO-03 oidc_pending, so retries and second tabs do not overwrite each other. A dedicated 1-minute sweeper replaces the earlier plan to use the hourly analytics retention ticker.

**Requirements**

- Migrations oauthbroker/0001 pending_authorizations(id 16 random bytes base64url PK, iss, sub, user_key, agent_id NULL, provider, scopes_json, message NULL, request_method NULL, request_host NULL, request_path NULL, mcp_tool NULL, status CHECK pending|granted|denied|expired, reason NULL, created_at, expires_at, completed_at NULL) indexed on (status, expires_at) and (user_key); oauthbroker/0002 connect_attempts(state_hash PK, pending_id NULL, iss, sub, user_key, provider, scopes_json, verifier, browser_hash, created_at, expires_at +10m); oauthbroker/0003 oauth_grants(user_key, iss, sub, provider, grant_id, state CHECK connecting|active|reconsent_required|revoked, scopes_json, provider_account_id NULL, provider_account_login NULL, granted_at, updated_at, last_used_at NULL, revoked_at NULL, UNIQUE(user_key, provider)).
- GrantStore methods (ctx, injectable now): CreatePending, GetPending (reports expired when expires_at <= now even before a sweep), CompletePending(id, status, reason) as compare-and-set from pending only (else ErrNotPending), CreateAttempt, ConsumeAttempt(stateHash) single use via DELETE ... RETURNING, BeginGrant (state=connecting, new grant_id), ActivateGrant(grantID, scopes, account), RevokeGrant(userKey, provider) idempotent, GetGrant, ListGrants(userKey, includeRevoked), TouchLastUsed(userKey, provider, at) at most one write per minute per pair (called by the W-P3-PUS-07 mint endpoint), Sweep(now).
- Notifier seam: Subscribe(id) (<-chan Status, cancel func()); the channel closes after CompletePending or expiry, so W-P3-JIT-04 attaches later and nothing here references JIT.
- Sweeper: started from the CP Server.Start only when the broker is enabled, every 1m; deletes expired attempts, marks expired pendings, deletes terminal pendings older than 7 days, and returns connecting grants older than 10m for the reconciler in W-P3-BRKR-04.
- Limits: at most 10,000 live attempts in total, 20 open attempts and 20 open pendings per user_key; beyond that ErrTooMany.
- No token, refresh token or client secret column or struct field exists; the verifier lives only in connect_attempts in the 0600 cpstate file and is never logged. Logs show pending ids and at most 8 hex chars of a state hash. With the broker disabled, no migrations run.

**Implementation plan**

1. New internal/oauthbroker/store.go: GrantStore interface, Pending, Attempt and Grant types, and the three Migration{ID, SQL} values passed to cpstate.Open from cmd/proxy/controlplane.go only when consent.providers is non-empty.
2. New internal/oauthbroker/store_sqlite.go: implementation over the cpstate DB, one statement per method, compare-and-set for CompletePending and DELETE ... RETURNING for ConsumeAttempt.
3. New internal/oauthbroker/notify.go: the Subscribe map, closed from CompletePending and Sweep.
4. New internal/oauthbroker/sweeper.go: RunSweeper(ctx, interval), started from controlplane Server.Start when the broker is enabled.
5. New internal/oauthbroker/oauthbrokertest/conformance.go: Run(t, newStore) covering every method.
6. Tests: store_test.go with a fake clock, a reflect test on Grant, Pending and Attempt, and a `PRAGMA table_info(oauth_grants)` column check.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] A pending past expires_at reads as expired before any sweep; after Sweep its stored status is expired and a Subscribe channel for it is closed within 1s. Verify with `go test ./internal/oauthbroker -run TestPendingExpiry`.
- [ ] Two concurrent CompletePending calls on one id give exactly one success; the other returns ErrNotPending.
- [ ] ConsumeAttempt returns an attempt once; a second call with the same state hash returns ErrNotFound.
- [ ] BeginGrant then ActivateGrant twice for the same (user_key, provider) leaves one row with a new grant_id and advanced updated_at; RevokeGrant twice succeeds.
- [ ] The 21st open pending for one user_key returns ErrTooMany, and no struct field or oauth_grants column is named or typed as a token, secret or value. Verify with `go test ./internal/oauthbroker/... -run TestGrantStoreConformance`.

### 3/9 · W-P3-BRKR-03

**Implement POST /connect/start with PKCE, CSRF and scope capping**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#135](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/135)

Add `POST /connect/start` on the CP behind the portal session middleware. It checks the block list, caps scopes against the provider and the pending row, creates a single-use attempt with state and PKCE S256, and redirects to the provider. A GET changes nothing and only redirects to the landing page, so a cross-site link cannot start a consent flow. The per-agent cap is applied when JIT creates the pending (W-P3-JIT-01), so this ticket needs no per-user-secrets dependency.

**Requirements**

- POST form fields provider, scopes (space separated), pending, csrf; CSRF is the portal session's X-Warden-CSRF value as header or `csrf` field, compared in constant time, and Origin, when present, must equal the portal origin (403 csrf). GET /connect/start returns 303 to /portal/connect/<pending> or /portal and writes nothing.
- Authentication: W-P3-CSIG-04 portal session middleware; no session gives 303 to /portal/login with a relative next; console sessions, worker tokens and API keys get 401.
- Block list: an oauthbroker-owned BlockChecker implemented in internal/controlplane over controlplane.BlockStore and its snapshot (the W-P2-TOKX-02 pattern), matching sub exactly and lowercase email only when verified; a match gives 403 user_blocked and a read error gives 503, in both cases before any row is written.
- Scopes: with a pending, it must belong to the session's (iss, sub) (otherwise 404 with a body identical to an unknown id), be status pending and unexpired (else 409 pending_not_active), and requested scopes must be a subset of pending.scopes; without a pending, requested scopes must be a subset of allowedScopes and of an optional caller-supplied ceiling (the portal passes allowedScopes ∩ the union of perUserSecrets scopes, W-P3-PORT-03), or defaultScopes are used. Any scope outside the cap gives 400 scope_not_allowed listing the names, before any row is written. The provider request asks for the union of the active grant's scopes and the capped scopes.
- Attempt: 32-byte random state (only SHA-256 stored), oauth2.GenerateVerifier with S256 challenge, and a `__Host-warden_connect` cookie (Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Path=/, Max-Age 600) whose hash is stored as browser_hash. Redirect 303 with Cache-Control: no-store and Referrer-Policy: no-referrer; extraAuthParams are appended; githubApp sends no scope parameter.
- Limits: 10 starts per minute per user_key using the W-P2-TOKX-04 token bucket, moved without behaviour change into new leaf package internal/ratelimit so oauthbroker does not import tokensvc (W-P3-PUS-07 and W-P3-JIT-01 reuse it) (429 with Retry-After); ErrTooMany from the store gives 429. No outbound network I/O in this handler.
- Gate: /connect/* is mounted only when the broker is enabled (providers set, cpstate open, persistent consent.store); otherwise 404. Providers configured with no consent.store or an echo one fail CP startup with `oauth broker requires a persistent consent.store`.
- Observability: log line `msg=oauth_connect_start provider user_key pending_id scopes_count outcome reason` (never state, verifier or challenge) and counter warden_cp_oauth_connect_total{provider,stage="start",outcome}.

**Implementation plan**

1. New internal/oauthbroker/server.go: Broker{reg, store, blocks BlockChecker, limiter, cfg, now}, New(...), the exported Start(ctx, StartRequest) (redirectURL string, err error) shared with the portal JSON actions, and Handler() mounting /connect/start (and /connect/callback in W-P3-BRKR-04).
2. New internal/oauthbroker/start.go: handleStart with the check order above, CreateAttempt, the cookie and the AuthCodeURL built with oauth2.Config, oauth2.S256ChallengeOption and SetAuthURLParam.
3. internal/controlplane: new blockchecker adapter over BlockStore for oauthbroker.BlockChecker, and mounting of the broker handler in the CP mux only when enabled.
4. cmd/proxy/controlplane.go: build the Registry and GrantStore, refuse startup for a missing or echo consent.store when providers are set, and wire the broker. Move the W-P2-TOKX-04 token bucket into new internal/ratelimit and point internal/tokensvc at it.
5. Tests in internal/oauthbroker/start_test.go and a controlplane wiring test for the startup refusal and the 404 when disabled.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] A signed-in user with a valid CSRF token posting provider=google with allowed scopes gets 303; the Location carries code_challenge_method=S256, a code_challenge equal to base64url(SHA-256(stored verifier)), a state whose SHA-256 equals the stored hash, exactly the capped scopes and the configured redirect_uri, and __Host-warden_connect is set. Verify with `go test ./internal/oauthbroker -run TestConnectStart`.
- [ ] A scope outside allowedScopes (or outside pending.scopes) returns 400 scope_not_allowed and connect_attempts and pending_authorizations gain zero rows.
- [ ] A pending owned by another (iss, sub) returns 404 byte-identical to an unknown id, and a blocked user gets 403 user_blocked with no row written.
- [ ] GET writes nothing and returns 303; a POST without valid CSRF returns 403; no session gives 303 to /portal/login; the 11th start in a minute returns 429.
- [ ] With providers set and no consent.store or an echo one, CP startup fails with the documented error; with no providers, /connect/start returns 404. Verify with `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestOAuthBrokerGate`.

### 4/9 · W-P3-BRKR-04

**Implement /connect/callback and write tokens to the secret backend**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#136](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/136)

Add `GET /connect/callback`: consume the attempt once, require the same browser and portal user, exchange the code with the PKCE verifier, and write a versioned TokenRecord to `secrets.UserGrantKey(userKey, provider)` in consent.store. The grants row is written as `connecting` before the secret and set `active` after it, so a failed step never leaves a token the portal cannot see or revoke; a reconciler cleans up rows stuck in `connecting`. Connect events go to admin audit without any secret reference.

**Requirements**

- Consume the attempt by SHA-256(state); unknown, expired or replayed state, or a __Host-warden_connect hash mismatch, gives 400 state_invalid on a generic page. A portal session whose (iss, sub) differs from the attempt gives 403 before any code exchange; no session gives a 401 page and the code is not stored. The block list is re-checked before the exchange.
- Exchange with oauth2.Config.Exchange and oauth2.VerifierOption, through an http.Client that sends Accept: application/json, has a 10s timeout, follows no redirects and caps responses at 64 KiB. A response with an `error` field (GitHub returns these with HTTP 200), an empty access_token or a non-bearer token_type is a failure. error=access_denied marks the pending denied; invalid_grant and other errors fail only this attempt and the pending stays open. Provider error text is never echoed to the user.
- Scopes: parse the returned scope (spaces or commas; absent means the requested set). Granted scopes outside the cap plus openid and email give scope_exceeded, nothing stored, WARN logged. Granted scopes missing requested ones are stored as returned and the pending is completed denied with reason insufficient_scope.
- Write order under oauthbroker.GrantLocks (new, one mutex per (userKey, provider), shared with W-P3-PUS-03, W-P3-PORT-02 and W-P3-OFFB-01): BeginGrant (connecting, new grant_id); consent.store Put of TokenRecord {v:1, grant_id, provider, client_id, token_type, access_token, refresh_token, scope, expiry absolute UTC or 0, refresh_expiry, obtained_at}, keeping the stored refresh_token when the response has none; ActivateGrant; re-check the block list and, if blocked, delete the key and revoke the grant; CompletePending(granted). The previous token is never revoked at the provider on reconnect.
- If Put fails, the token is dropped from memory, the grant stays connecting and the page returns 503 secret_store_unavailable. The sweeper's connecting grants older than 10m are reconciled by deleting the key if present and marking the grant revoked; an hourly pass counts keys under users/ with no active grant into an orphan gauge.
- Audit: when admin audit is enabled, an unhealthy Recorder gives 503 admin_audit_unavailable before the exchange; connect.granted and connect.denied are recorded with actor = portal sub, auth_method `portal` (new value), target `grant:<provider>`, target_ref `grant_id:<id>`, details {provider, scopes, pending_id}. A slog line `msg=connect schema=warden.consent.v1` is always written. No secrets.Ref, token, code, state or verifier appears in any row or line.
- On success, 303 to fixed internal paths only: /portal/connect/<pending>?result=granted or /portal?connected=<provider>. Counters warden_cp_oauth_connect_total{stage="callback"} and warden_cp_oauth_token_exchange_seconds{provider}.

**Implementation plan**

1. New internal/oauthbroker/callback.go: handleCallback with the checks, exchange, scope handling and write order above.
2. New internal/oauthbroker/exchange.go: the provider http.Client (dials through proxy.NewSafeDialer from internal/proxy/safedial.go so generic provider URLs cannot reach private addresses; tests inject a client) and the error-field check.
3. New internal/oauthbroker/reconcile.go: reconciler run from the W-P3-BRKR-02 sweeper; new internal/oauthbroker/locks.go: GrantLocks.
4. internal/adminaudit: add `portal` to the validated auth_method set.
5. New test/fakes/oauthprovider.go (httptest authorize and token endpoints with PKCE check, Google-style JSON and GitHub-style comma scopes and 200-with-error); tests use fakes.MemorySecretStore from W-P3-CSIG-06 as consent.store.
6. Tests in internal/oauthbroker/callback_test.go, including a log and audit capture test.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Start then callback against fakes.OAuthProvider leaves fakes.MemorySecretStore holding users/<userKey>/google with the fake's access_token and a grant_id equal to the active grants row, the pending granted, and its Subscribe channel closed within 1s. Verify with `go test ./internal/oauthbroker -run TestConnectCallback`.
- [ ] A callback with a valid state but a different portal user returns 403, the fake token endpoint receives 0 requests and the store and grants stay empty; replaying a used state returns 400 state_invalid.
- [ ] error=access_denied sets the pending denied and records connect.denied; a GitHub-style HTTP 200 with error=bad_verification_code writes no secret and leaves the pending open.
- [ ] A reconnect whose response lacks refresh_token keeps the previously stored refresh_token; a granted scope outside the cap writes no secret and no active grant.
- [ ] With fakes.MemorySecretStore set to fail Put, the response is 503 secret_store_unavailable and after the reconciler runs the grant is revoked and no key exists.
- [ ] Logs and audit rows across all cases contain no access token, refresh token, code, state, verifier or `sha256:` reference. Verify with `go test ./internal/oauthbroker -run TestCallbackNoSecretLeak`.

**Depends on:** [`W-P3-BRKR-03`](oauth-broker.md#39--w-p3-brkr-03) Implement POST /connect/start with PKCE, CSRF and scope capping; [`W-P1-AAUD-01`](admin-audit-log.md#14--w-p1-aaud-01) Add signed, hash-chained admin audit store on cpstate

### 5/9 · W-P3-BRKR-05

**Add provider revoke client for Google and GitHub**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#137](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/137)

Add `oauthbroker.Revoke(ctx, provider, rec TokenRecord)` for Google, GitHub, GitHub Apps and RFC 7009 generic providers. It only calls the provider; deleting the secret and the grant row stays with W-P3-PORT-02 RevokeUserGrant and W-P3-OFFB-01. It is a pure library, so it can be built in parallel with the HTTP tickets.

**Requirements**

- Google: POST revokeURL form-encoded token=<refresh_token>, falling back to access_token; 200 is success and 400 invalid_token counts as already revoked.
- github and githubApp: DELETE revokeURL (default https://api.github.com/applications/{client_id}/grant) with basic auth clientID:clientSecret, JSON body {"access_token":...}, Accept: application/vnd.github+json; any 2xx is success, 404 is already revoked, 422 is a permanent error. Document that this removes every token of that app for the user.
- generic: RFC 7009 POST token plus token_type_hint=refresh_token with client_secret_basic; no revokeURL returns ErrRevokeUnsupported with no HTTP call, so callers still delete the stored secret.
- Errors: *RevokeError{Provider, Status, Retryable}; network errors, 429 and 5xx are retryable, 401 and 403 are not. 10s timeout, no redirects, response read capped at 16 KiB; error strings never contain the token or the response body.
- Observability: counter warden_cp_oauth_revoke_total{provider,outcome=ok|already|retryable|failed|unsupported} and `msg=oauth_revoke provider user_key status outcome duration_ms`, never the token.

**Implementation plan**

1. New internal/oauthbroker/revoke.go: Revoke, RevokeError and ErrRevokeUnsupported, using the provider http.Client shape from W-P3-BRKR-01 config (injectable for tests).
2. Per-type request builders for google, github/githubApp and generic in the same file.
3. Tests: internal/oauthbroker/revoke_test.go with httptest servers for each provider type and a log-capture check.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] The fake Google endpoint receives form-encoded token equal to the refresh token, or the access token when the refresh token is empty. Verify with `go test ./internal/oauthbroker -run TestRevokeGoogle`.
- [ ] The fake GitHub endpoint receives DELETE /applications/<client_id>/grant with client basic auth and an access_token JSON body, and 204 returns nil. Verify with `go test ./internal/oauthbroker -run TestRevokeGitHub`.
- [ ] Google 400 invalid_token and GitHub 404 return nil and record outcome=already.
- [ ] A 503 returns RevokeError with Retryable=true and a 401 returns Retryable=false.
- [ ] A generic provider without revokeURL returns ErrRevokeUnsupported and the fake receives no request; no token substring appears in logs or error strings.

**Depends on:** [`W-P3-BRKR-01`](oauth-broker.md#19--w-p3-brkr-01) Add provider config model with Google and GitHub defaults

**Unblocks:** [`W-P3-BRKR-08`](oauth-broker.md#89--w-p3-brkr-08) Record the connected provider account and enforce account rules; [`W-P3-PORT-02`](consent-portal.md#27--w-p3-port-02) Implement revoke with grant, secret, epoch and provider steps

### 6/9 · W-P3-BRKR-06

**Guard reserved prefixes on the worker dashboard and load client secrets from consent.store**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#279](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/279)

W-P3-CSIG-06 owns the reserved prefixes (`users/`, `idp/`, `revoking/`, `oauth-clients/`) and enforces them in config validation, storeFetcher and /central/secrets. This ticket covers the remaining write surface, the dashboard secret-store tab (/dashboard/api/secretstore), and resolves provider client secrets from consent.store at `oauth-clients/<id>`, so a client secret never sits in the store whose credential the CP sends to workers. Operators load client secrets directly in the backend or use clientSecretEnv; no console path writes them.

**Requirements**

- /dashboard/api/secretstore POST and DELETE return 403 {"error":"reserved_key"} for keys where secrets.IsReservedKey is true, and its List hides them, matching the W-P3-CSIG-06 /central/secrets behaviour.
- clientSecretKey must equal secrets.ClientSecretKey(id). The Registry's SecretResolver reads it from consent.store at startup; a read failure logs WARN with the key only and is retried on first use (503 provider_unavailable). It is never read from the distributed secretStore.
- No flag or route writes `oauth-clients/` keys through /central/secrets or the dashboard; docs/consent-portal.md (W-P3-PORT-04) gives the aws secretsmanager and vault kv commands for loading them.
- The broker, the W-P3-PUS-03 refresh engine and W-P3-OFFB-01 use consent.store directly and are not affected by the guard.
- With no reserved keys in use, every existing request and config behaves exactly as before.

**Implementation plan**

1. internal/dashboard/dashboard_v3.go: enforce secrets.IsReservedKey in handleSecretStore for writes, deletes and List.
2. internal/oauthbroker/provider.go: a SecretResolver over consent.store and the clientSecretKey rule; cmd/proxy/controlplane.go passes the consent.store built by W-P3-CSIG-06.
3. Tests in internal/dashboard and internal/oauthbroker.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] POST and DELETE /dashboard/api/secretstore for `users/x/google` and `oauth-clients/google` return 403 reserved_key and the store is unchanged, and its List omits reserved keys while still listing other keys. Verify with `go test ./internal/dashboard -run TestSecretStoreReservedKey`.
- [ ] A google provider with clientSecretKey `oauth-clients/google` resolves its secret from a fake consent.store and never calls the distributed secretStore; clientSecretKey `oauth-clients/other` for provider google fails validation. Verify with `go test ./internal/oauthbroker -run TestClientSecretFromUserStore`.
- [ ] A failed read at startup logs only the key, and the first connect returns 503 provider_unavailable.

**Depends on:** [`W-P3-CSIG-06`](consent-auth.md#67--w-p3-csig-06) Add the CP-only user credential store, user key helpers and reserved secret prefixes; [`W-P3-BRKR-01`](oauth-broker.md#19--w-p3-brkr-01) Add provider config model with Google and GitHub defaults; [`W-P1-SSO-06`](console-sso-rbac.md#68--w-p1-sso-06) Require an admin session on /central/secrets and flag open consoles

### 7/9 · W-P3-BRKR-07

**Add the provider refresh-token client for CP-side refresh**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#280](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/280)

The CP is the only refresh authority (W-P3-PUS-03): workers never receive provider metadata, client secrets or refresh tokens, so no provider projection goes on /policy. Add the provider HTTP client for the refresh_token grant next to the code exchange (W-P3-BRKR-04) and revoke (W-P3-BRKR-05) clients, so every call to a provider token endpoint lives in internal/oauthbroker with the same hardening. It is a pure library; the W-P3-PUS-03 engine calls it.

**Requirements**

- `oauthbroker.Refresh(ctx, provider, rec TokenRecord, clientSecret) (TokenRecord, error)` posts grant_type=refresh_token to provider.TokenURL with client_secret_basic for google and generic and client_secret_post for github and githubApp, with Accept: application/json.
- The HTTP client is https only except loopback, dials through proxy.NewSafeDialer so generic provider URLs cannot reach private addresses, follows no redirects, has a 5s timeout and caps responses at 64 KiB. A 200 with an `error` field is a failure.
- The returned record keeps the stored refresh_token when the response has none, sets expiry from expires_in against local receipt time, sets refresh_expiry when the provider returns one, and keeps grant_id, provider and client_id.
- Errors form a closed set: ErrRefreshInvalidGrant for invalid_grant, a permanent error for other 4xx, and a retryable error for 429, 5xx and network failures. Only the OAuth `error` code is kept, never error_description or the body.
- A record with expiry 0 and no refresh_token (GitHub OAuth app) returns ErrNotRefreshable with no HTTP call.
- Counter warden_cp_oauth_refresh_total{provider,outcome}; no token or client secret appears in logs or error strings.

**Implementation plan**

1. New internal/oauthbroker/refresh.go: Refresh, the error values and a request builder per provider type, using the provider http.Client shape from W-P3-BRKR-01 config (injectable for tests).
2. Add the counter next to the other oauthbroker counters.
3. Tests: internal/oauthbroker/refresh_test.go with httptest token endpoints for each provider type and a log-capture check.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] The fake Google endpoint receives grant_type=refresh_token with client basic auth; a response without refresh_token keeps the stored one and a rotated one is returned. Verify with `go test ./internal/oauthbroker -run TestRefreshGoogle`.
- [ ] A GitHub App refresh sends client_secret_post and a response with refresh_token_expires_in sets refresh_expiry. Verify with `go test ./internal/oauthbroker -run TestRefreshGitHubApp`.
- [ ] invalid_grant returns ErrRefreshInvalidGrant, 503 is retryable, a 200 with error=bad_refresh_token is a failure, and a GitHub OAuth-app record makes no HTTP call.
- [ ] No log line or error string contains a token, the client secret or the response body.

**Depends on:** [`W-P3-BRKR-01`](oauth-broker.md#19--w-p3-brkr-01) Add provider config model with Google and GitHub defaults

**Unblocks:** [`W-P3-BRKR-09`](oauth-broker.md#99--w-p3-brkr-09) Add end-to-end OAuth broker test with fake Google and GitHub; [`W-P3-PUS-03`](refresh-model.md#312--w-p3-pus-03) Implement the CP user-token refresh engine

### 8/9 · W-P3-BRKR-08

**Record the connected provider account and enforce account rules**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#281](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/281)

Nothing records which external account was connected, so a user could connect a personal Gmail or another person's GitHub account and agents would act on it. After the code exchange, identify the account, store it on the grant, and enforce the optional allowedAccountDomains and requireEmailMatch rules before the token is written.

**Requirements**

- Google: add `openid email` to the request (exempt from the scope cap) and read sub, email, email_verified and hd from the id_token returned directly by the token endpoint over TLS, checking iss and aud=clientID; set the `hd` auth param when allowedAccountDomains has one entry.
- github and githubApp: GET userinfoURL (default https://api.github.com/user) with the new token and read id, login and email; generic: use userinfoURL when set, else record nothing.
- allowedAccountDomains: the account email domain (or Google hd) must match; requireEmailMatch: the account email must equal the portal session's verified email, case-insensitive. A mismatch completes the pending denied with reason account_not_allowed, drops the token and revokes it with W-P3-BRKR-05, and writes no secret.
- provider_account_id and provider_account_login (the GitHub login, or the Google account email) are stored on the grant and added to the connect.granted audit details; the portal shows provider_account_login to its owner as account_label (W-P3-PORT-01), and the portal session email is not stored.
- With neither rule set, identification failures are logged and the connect proceeds; with a rule set, failure to identify denies.

**Implementation plan**

1. New internal/oauthbroker/account.go: Identify(ctx, provider, token) (Account, error) per type.
2. internal/oauthbroker/callback.go: call Identify before BeginGrant and enforce the rules; pass the account to ActivateGrant.
3. test/fakes/oauthprovider.go: add an id_token and a /user endpoint to the fake.
4. Tests in internal/oauthbroker/account_test.go.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] A fake Google id_token with hd=example.com connects when allowedAccountDomains=[example.com] and the grant records the provider account id. Verify with `go test ./internal/oauthbroker -run TestAccountRules`.
- [ ] An account with hd=gmail.com, or an email different from the session's with requireEmailMatch, gives denied account_not_allowed, no secret written and one revoke request at the fake.
- [ ] A GitHub connect stores the /user id and login on the grant.

**Depends on:** [`W-P3-BRKR-04`](oauth-broker.md#49--w-p3-brkr-04) Implement /connect/callback and write tokens to the secret backend; [`W-P3-BRKR-05`](oauth-broker.md#59--w-p3-brkr-05) Add provider revoke client for Google and GitHub

**Unblocks:** [`W-P3-BRKR-09`](oauth-broker.md#99--w-p3-brkr-09) Add end-to-end OAuth broker test with fake Google and GitHub; [`W-P3-PORT-01`](consent-portal.md#17--w-p3-port-01) Serve the portal page and the connections list API

### 9/9 · W-P3-BRKR-09

**Add end-to-end OAuth broker test with fake Google and GitHub**

Type **test** · Size **M** · Issue [#282](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/282)

Every other ticket tests one handler. This test runs a real CP with consent sign-in, the broker and the AWS secret store over a fake AWS client, plus fake Google and GitHub providers, and proves the done_when sentence including the refusal cases. It runs behind the existing integration build tag, so normal `go test ./...` is unaffected.

**Requirements**

- Happy path for google and github: portal login, POST /connect/start, provider redirect, callback; the fake AWS client behind consent.store holds `warden-cp/users/<userKey>/<provider>` with a versioned token JSON, and nothing is written under the distributed secretStore prefix.
- Refusals with no secret written: callback from another portal session, blocked user, scope outside the cap, replayed state, account outside allowedAccountDomains, missing or echo consent.store at startup.
- Reconnect without refresh_token keeps the stored refresh_token; /central/secrets writes under users/ return 403 reserved_key; a stored grant refreshes through the W-P3-BRKR-07 client against the fake provider.
- After all cases, a byte scan of the cpstate file finds no access or refresh token, and a log scan finds no token, code, state or verifier.
- Runs without Docker or network access to real providers.

**Implementation plan**

1. New test/integration/oauthbroker_test.go under the integration build tag.
2. Reuse test/fakes.OAuthProvider and the fake IdP from the consent sign-in tests; add a fake AWSSecretsClient if one is not already in test/fakes.
3. Add a manual check list for a real Google Web client, a GitHub OAuth App and a GitHub App to the W-P3-PORT-04 guide notes, including whether GitHub accepts PKCE for each app type (state, the browser cookie and the session binding protect the flow either way).

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] `go test -tags integration ./test/integration -run TestOAuthBrokerE2E` passes.
- [ ] The test fails if any refusal case writes a secret or a grant in state active.
- [ ] The cpstate byte scan and the log scan find no token, code, state or verifier.

**Depends on:** [`W-P3-BRKR-06`](oauth-broker.md#69--w-p3-brkr-06) Guard reserved prefixes on the worker dashboard and load client secrets from consent.store; [`W-P3-BRKR-07`](oauth-broker.md#79--w-p3-brkr-07) Add the provider refresh-token client for CP-side refresh; [`W-P3-BRKR-08`](oauth-broker.md#89--w-p3-brkr-08) Record the connected provider account and enforce account rules
